journal_name: Journal of Electronic Testing-Theory and Applications

abstracts.abstract: This paper presents a novel paradigm for test generation in complex integrated circuits by establishing a theoretical framework based on graph neural networks and fault propagation analysis. Traditional test generation methods rely heavily on deterministic algorithms that struggle to capture the intricate relationships between circuit topology and fault effects. The proposed Graph-Based Test Generation Framework (GTGF) models the circuit under test as a heterogeneous graph where nodes represent circuit elements and edges encode both structural and functional connectivity. By introducing attention mechanisms into message passing neural networks, the framework learns to predict test point effectiveness and generate high-quality test patterns without explicit fault simulation. Theoretical analysis proves that GTGF can approximate optimal test generation with polynomial complexity for circuits with bounded treewidth. Experimental results on ISCAS'89 and ITC'99 benchmark circuits demonstrate that the proposed paradigm achieves 23% higher fault coverage compared to state-of-the-art deterministic ATPG while reducing test generation time by 67%. This work fundamentally transforms the test generation problem from an algorithmic search into a learned prediction task, opening new research directions at the intersection of machine learning and VLSI testing. The theoretical contributions establish formal bounds on learnability of testability properties and provide a foundation for future data-driven testing approaches.

Built-in self-test has emerged as an essential technique for testing complex system-on-chip devices, yet existing analytical models for BIST test length optimization fail to accurately predict the number of patterns required to achieve target reliability levels in modern nanoscale designs. This paper presents an enhanced probabilistic framework for determining optimal BIST parameters based on a more sophisticated fault coverage model that accounts for correlation effects between test patterns. The proposed approach extends classical statistical test theory by introducing a Markov chain-based dependency model that captures how the detectability of faults changes as test patterns are applied sequentially. We derive closed-form expressions for the expected fault coverage as a function of test length, pattern distribution, and circuit-specific parameters. The analytical framework provides precise guidelines for selecting linear feedback shift register configurations and test mode configurations in designs with multiple test modes. Validation using industrial designs with up to 50 million gates demonstrates that the analytical predictions deviate from actual measurements by less than 3%, compared to 15-20% error with existing models. The improved accuracy enables designers to reduce BIST overhead by 18% while maintaining equivalent test quality, resulting in significant reductions in test time and cost without compromising product quality.

Testing three-dimensional integrated circuits presents unprecedented challenges that cannot be adequately addressed by conventional planar test architectures. This paper introduces a comprehensive test architecture for 3D ICs that fundamentally reconceptualizes how test access mechanisms and test scheduling are implemented across multiple die layers. The proposed Modular 3D Test Architecture (M3DTA) introduces die-level test wrappers with through-silicon via awareness and an adaptive test bus structure that dynamically reconfigures based on detected defects. Unlike previous approaches that treat each die independently, M3DTA implements a hierarchical test controller that coordinates pre-bond, mid-bond, and post-bond test phases while optimizing for yield learning and test time reduction. The architecture includes novel defect isolation mechanisms that leverage the inherent layering structure of 3D ICs to achieve precise defect localization. A complete EDA flow has been developed to automatically generate M3DTA-compliant designs from RTL specifications. Implementation results on a 2.5D interposer test vehicle and a prototype 3D stacked memory device demonstrate that M3DTA achieves 40% reduction in test time compared to current industrial approaches while enabling 95% defect localization accuracy. The architectural paradigm supports arbitrary 3D stacking configurations and provides a scalable foundation for future 3D IC test methodology development.

Memory testing remains a critical bottleneck in manufacturing test flows for systems containing large embedded memory arrays, as traditional March-based test algorithms incur substantial test time overhead. This paper presents an enhanced memory BIST architecture that significantly improves test efficiency through a novel adaptive test engine capable of dynamically adjusting test patterns based on real-time fault detection. The proposed March-Adaptive BIST (MA-BIST) system integrates configurable March test primitives with an on-chip diagnosis unit that identifies emerging fault patterns and selects optimized test sequences from a pre-synthesized library. The architecture features a patented test scheduling mechanism that exploits memory independence to enable parallel testing of multiple memory instances, reducing overall test time by up to 55% compared to conventional serial BIST approaches. Hardware implementation results in 65nm CMOS technology demonstrate that MA-BIST occupies only 8% area overhead while supporting 127 different test algorithms including all standard March tests plus custom defect-oriented tests. The system achieves complete coverage of commonly modeled memory faults including coupling, address decoder, and retention faults. Industrial validation on DRAM and SRAM macros confirms test time reductions averaging 48% with no degradation in defect escape rates, validating the practical viability of adaptive memory testing in production environments.
